titulo_en: I could ride a bike when I was five

texto.@es: **Could + verbo base**: **I could swim when I was five** (sabía nadar cuando tenía cinco años). No cambia con he, she o they. Para negar, **couldn't + verbo base**.
texto.@en: **Could + verbo base**: **I could swim when I was five** (I knew how to swim when I was five). It doesn't change with him, he or they. To deny, **couldn't + verbo base**.

texto.@es: **Could you read when you were six?** (¿sabías leer cuando tenías seis años?). Para una habilidad actual, usa **can**: **I can ride a bike now**.
texto.@en: **Could you read when you were six?** (did you know how to read when you were six?). For a current skill, use **can**: **I can ride a bike now**.

texto.@es: **Could** suele describir una capacidad general en el pasado. Para decir que conseguiste algo en una ocasión concreta, normalmente usa **was/were able to** o **managed to**: **I was able to repair my bike yesterday** (conseguí reparar mi bicicleta ayer). **Couldn't** también puede describir un intento concreto que no salió bien.
texto.@en: **Could** usually describes a general capacity in the past. To say that you got something on a specific occasion, you usually use **was/were able to** or **managed to**: **I was able to repair my bike yesterday** (I managed to repair my bike yesterday). **Couldn't** can also describe a concrete attempt that didn't work out.

intro.@es: **Could** también habla de una capacidad general en el pasado. Para decir que antes podías o sabías hacer algo, usa **could**; para decir que no podías, usa **couldn't**.
intro.@en: **Could** also speaks of a general capacity in the past. To say that you could or knew how to do something before, use **could**; to say you couldn't, use **couldn't**.
